elements.label: Hộp 5
elements.title: Ô nhiễm không khí ở Hà Nội: Hành động có mục tiêu có thể tối đa hóa lợi ích kép như thế nào
elements.content:
Text box describing air pollution in Hanoi and targeted actions to maximize co-benefits from decarbonization.

Main points transcribed:
- Vietnam’s main national benefit from decarbonization is reduced air pollution, especially in Hanoi and surrounding provinces.
- Current air quality requires urgent action to reduce pollution levels and people’s exposure to harmful PM2.5.
- The annual average concentration measured is clearly above the national air quality standard (NAAQS) of 25 µg/m³ and above the World Health Organization guideline of 10 µg/m³.
- PM2.5 in Hanoi comes from both local and neighboring areas.
- A recent World Bank analysis identified the main sources as:
  (i) nearly 35% from industry, including power plants and large industrial facilities around Hanoi;
  (ii) about 25% from transport;
  (iii) 20% related to ammonia emissions from livestock and fertilizer use;
  (iv) 10% from residential emissions (mainly biomass cooking);
  (v) about 7% from open burning of agricultural waste.
- PM2.5 concentrations are projected to continue rising, mainly due to planned coal capacity expansion without stronger air pollution regulations.
- According to the Government’s plan, 10 new coal-fired power plants will come into operation in the northern region by 2030.
- Agricultural pollution is expected to increase due to higher output and lack of policies addressing ammonia emissions.
- Improving Hanoi’s air quality requires urgent, closely coordinated action with neighboring provinces.
- Priority actions should include: reducing dependence on coal, for example by repurposing the 100 MV plant in Ninh Binh; encouraging farmers to use less polluting inputs and burn less waste; improving public transport; and applying stricter vehicle emissions standards.

Source line:
Nguồn: Ngân hàng Thế giới, 2021, “Nguồn tích tụ gây ô nhiễm không khí ở Hà Nội, chưa xuất bản.”

Visible text labels/numbers: PM2.5; NAAQS 25 µg/m³; 10 µg/m³; 35%; 25%; 20%; 10%; 7%; 10 nhà máy; 2030; 100 MV; Ninh Bình.
